analysis: The trial completed successfully but reduced pinned-host macro validation HR@10 to 0.4437, versus 0.470 for the preceding normalized-candidate model and 0.505 for the baseline. Category HR@10: Movies_and_TV 0.530, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.460, Electronics 0.305, CDs_and_Vinyl 0.480. Removing candidate normalization did not improve Electronics, which remained at 0.305. This experiment does not support raw candidate embedding magnitudes as a remedy; the results do not establish the underlying cause of the performance gap. No held-out test results were available.
code_summary: Trained one independent model per category with tied input/output embeddings, two causal attention blocks, four attention heads, 128-dimensional embeddings, and 100-item histories. Last-state, mean, and two recency-aware attention pools produce a normalized context. Scoring uses raw candidate embeddings, a learned scale clamped to [1,40], and jointly trained item bias. Retained 64-negative sampled-softmax training, AdamW, seed 42, validation checkpoint selection, and existing training controls. Each routed predictor loads one selected checkpoint and calls the shared architecture; verification checks strict loading, tied embeddings, explicit raw-embedding scores, and generated-predictor parity. No ensembles or separately fitted scoring components.
